purpose: authority-guided research redirection after rejection of the global next-origin learned hazard: test a simple role-preserving sequential multi-state detector with explicit recovery and a classical one-sided CUSUM structural monitor
upper_problem_definition: online health-state monitoring with sparse structural-break events, heterogeneous multi-clock evidence, nuisance-alarm control, recovery from aborted warnings, and transition-specific roles rather than homogeneous next-horizon voting

authority_basis.reference: Putter, Fiocco and Geskus (2007), Tutorial in biostatistics: competing risks and multi-state models
authority_basis.use: intermediate states and transition-specific modeling rather than one global binary outcome

authority_basis.reference: Jackson (2011), Multi-State Models for Panel Data: The msm Package for R
authority_basis.use: multi-state transition structure with time-varying covariates
explicit state-duration concept; in this V1 duration is tracked but not statistically fitted because event support is sparse

authority_basis.reference: Xie, Zou, Xie and Veeravalli (2021), Sequential (Quickest) Change Detection: Classical Results and New Directions
authority_basis.use: online change detection framing and delay-versus-false-alarm trade-off
tabular CUSUM design guidance: k approximately half a 1-sigma target shift and h around 4 or 5; V1 freezes k=0.5 and h=5 primary, h=4 sensitivity-only before scoring

authority_basis.reference: ISA-18.2 alarm-management guidance as summarized by ISA InTech
authority_basis.use: avoid nuisance/chattering alarms through explicit alarm logic; V1 adds no new tuned persistence because FAST already has frozen two-observation persistence and the state machine has explicit recovery/de-escalation

authority_basis.reference: Riley et al. (2019), Minimum sample size for developing a multivariable prediction model: Part II
authority_basis.use: sparse event support argues against high-dimensional fitted probability models after the 15-event Phase-A evaluation window

primary_model.type: deterministic role-preserving sequential finite-state detector with causal one-sided adverse CUSUM

inputs.FAST: tactical weakening/alert evidence on its frozen daily rule
inputs.SLOW: confirmation/new-regime evidence on its frozen completed-week rule
inputs.LAGGED_SIGMA20: lagged 20-governed-observation return volatility from the frozen event contract, used only to standardize current return for CUSUM; adverse_fraction and threshold progress are forbidden as predictors
inputs.CURRENT_REGIME: causally maintained regime direction after confirmed breaks

excluded_primary_inputs.EMERGENCY_REVERSAL: WP3 same-origin review found no incremental early-warning detection/recall gain over FAST and higher false-warning burden
excluded_primary_inputs.BOCPD_RETURN_SUCCESSOR_V1: native completed-month regime context; not a daily trigger
excluded_primary_inputs.MONTHLY_H1_AND_MONTHLY_DIRECTION: strategic context only, independent of short-term trigger
excluded_primary_inputs.GVZ_MACRO_MARKET_SHOCK_EXPERT_CHANNELS: optional/partial blocks deferred until an accepted WP4 core exists
excluded_primary_inputs.ADVERSE_FRACTION: direct anatomy/progress measure derived from the same price path as the event label; forbidden from primary predictive evidence

cusum_rule.adverse_evidence: a_t = -z_t in current UP regime; a_t = z_t in current DOWN regime
cusum_rule.reset: G_t resets to 0 on a confirmed frozen WP2 break; favorable evidence naturally drives the one-sided statistic toward zero

transition_rules_primary_h5.global_priority: if the frozen current-origin break condition is met, emit CONFIRMED_BREAK immediately, update current regime to the event new regime, reset CUSUM, and count any missing pre-break warning honestly

STABLE.to_WEAKENING: FAST conflicts with the current regime OR adverse CUSUM G_t >= 5

WEAKENING.to_BREAK_ALERT: FAST is robustly opposite the current regime OR (FAST conflicts with current regime AND adverse CUSUM G_t >= 5)
WEAKENING.to_STABLE: FAST robustly supports the current regime AND adverse CUSUM G_t < 5

BREAK_ALERT.to_STABLE: FAST robustly supports current regime AND adverse CUSUM G_t < 5
BREAK_ALERT.to_WEAKENING: strong alert condition no longer holds but at least one weakening condition remains

CONFIRMED_BREAK.to_NEW_REGIME: SLOW robustly supports the new current regime on its completed-week clock

NEW_REGIME.to_STABLE: FAST and SLOW both robustly support the current new regime

ablation_and_sensitivity.WP4B_ROLE_FSM_NO_CUSUM: same state machine but CUSUM conditions disabled; scored as a preregistered structural ablation, not selected after results
ablation_and_sensitivity.WP4B_RP_CUSUM_FSM_H4_SENSITIVITY: identical to primary but h=4; sensitivity-only and cannot replace h=5 based on formation results

formation_interpretation_rule.anatomy_false_alarm_ceiling_reference: WP3 PATH_HALF false episodes per 100 origins = 5.698005698005698; this is an operational burden ceiling only, not predictive evidence
formation_interpretation_rule.positive_signal: primary h=5 candidate must have prebreak WEAKENING recall >= FAST_CONFLICT, median WEAKENING lead observations >= FAST_CONFLICT, false WEAKENING episodes per 100 <= 5.698005698005698, and must strictly improve at least one of recall or median lead; this is formation research support only, not promotion
formation_interpretation_rule.stronger_signal: if recall >= 0.50, median lead >= 1 governed origin and false warning burden stays <= 5.698005698005698, label FORMATION_STRONGER_SIGNAL
formation_interpretation_rule.negative_signal: if the primary h=5 candidate fails the positive_signal rule, close WP4B primary as NO_INCREMENTAL_VALUE; h=4 sensitivity cannot rescue it
formation_interpretation_rule.challenge_gate: 2025 remains locked until formation results are inspected and a separate manifest-authorized challenge step is created
